findings.behavioral_consequence: Because the tests only pin exact output numbers rather than the underlying mechanism, a regression that changes the discount computation (e.g. switches from a 10%-of-subtotal floor discount to an unrelated flat-1000-cent rebate, or shifts the threshold boundary while altering rounding) could still produce 9_999/9_000/9_001 for these specific inputs and pass undetected. Additionally, since none of the new tests combine the bulk threshold with CustomerTier.VIP, a defect in how bulk and tier discounts stack (e.g., double-discounting or discount being silently overridden) would not be caught by this test set, giving false confidence that bulk-discount boundary behavior is fully validated when only the non-VIP, single-item path is proven.
findings.concise_summary: The three new boundary tests (subtotalJustBelowThresholdHasNoDiscount, subtotalAtThresholdGetsBulkDiscount, subtotalJustAboveThresholdGetsBulkDiscount) verify only the single aggregate calculateTotalCents() return value at three subtotal points (9_999 -> 9_999, 10_000 -> 9_000, 10_001 -> 9_001). None of them assert the discount mechanism itself (e.g. a discount-applied flag, discount rate, or line-item breakdown), and none exercise the threshold in combination with a non-default CustomerTier, so the tests cannot distinguish 'correct bulk-threshold logic' from 'any other code path that coincidentally yields the same three numbers'.
